title: Browser cache, CDN and cache headers

videos.script:
The fastest request is the one that is never made. {{second}} A visitor who comes back already has most of the page: the script, the stylesheet, the pictures. Whether the browser uses what it has, asks whether it is still right, or downloads it all again is decided by a few headers the server sends, and the planner sends none of them.

{{rules}} You will give it two rules. A file whose name carries a hash of its contents is kept for a year without asking. Everything else is kept and checked, and the server answers a check with three bytes of status instead of the file.

{{edge}} Then a cache that is not the browser's: a small CDN of your own, in front of the planner, that keeps what the headers let it keep and says when it answered from its store. {{stale}} You will catch it serving a course under its old name, which is the price of every shared cache, and see how long that price lasts.

{{frameworks}} And last, what the four frameworks send without being asked.
